hero.title: Hormuz Shipping Falls Sharply as Canada and Europe Move Closer and Trump–Xi Prepare for Summit
hero.description: Global markets begin the week watching three major developments: sharply reduced shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, a proposed new Canada–EU relationship, and preparations for a major Trump–Xi meeting in Washington.

breaking: 🚨 HORMUZ: Only 12 commodity vessels crossed the Strait of Hormuz over the weekend, down from 35 the previous weekend and far below the roughly 125 large commercial vessels that normally crossed each day before the conflict.

🛢️ Oil has not stopped flowing completely. Some Middle Eastern tankers are reportedly operating with tracking transponders switched off, while Saudi crude exports through Hormuz have recovered to more than 4 million barrels per day in September.

🇨🇦🇪🇺 CANADA–EU: French President Emmanuel Macron has backed exploring Canada's proposed associate-member relationship with the European Union after meeting Prime Minister Mark Carney in Saint-Pierre and Miquelon.
🇨🇦🇫🇷 Canada and France have agreed to deepen cooperation in defence, energy, space, telecommunications, technology and other strategic areas.
⚠️ Canada is NOT joining the European Union. The proposed associate-member status would be a new arrangement and there is currently no established EU treaty framework for it.
🇺🇸🇨🇳 Donald Trump and Xi Jinping are preparing to meet in Washington on September 24, with trade, tariffs, technology, critical minerals, AI and other strategic issues expected to feature.
🇺🇸🇨🇳 US and Chinese officials have also agreed to begin a new dialogue on AI-related risks and national-security incidents ahead of the leaders' summit.
🇺🇳 Nearly 130 heads of state are expected in New York this week for the UN General Assembly, with conflicts, energy security, trade and AI among the major international issues.
🇷🇺🇺🇦 Russia says Ukraine launched a major drone attack around Moscow during the final day of Russia's parliamentary election. Russian authorities reported casualties and damage to an oil refinery.

🇳🇬 Dangote Industries has acquired 4,000 additional construction machines, bringing its refinery expansion fleet to about 6,500 machines as it prepares to increase refining capacity towards 1.4 million barrels per day.
🇳🇬 Dangote's IPO remains open at ₦525 per share for 4.1 billion shares, targeting about ₦2.15 trillion, or approximately $1.6 billion.

🌍 A proposed Dangote regional fuel-distribution pipeline across Southern Africa has also been reported, with an estimated value of about $3.5 billion. The proposal remains subject to development and financing.

featured.title: Hormuz Shipping Falls to a Trickle, but Middle East Oil Flows Continue
featured.content: The Strait of Hormuz remains at the centre of the global energy crisis. Preliminary Kpler data shows that only 12 commodity vessels crossed the waterway over the weekend, compared with 35 the previous weekend and roughly 125 large commercial vessels per day before the conflict. The decline is significant, but it does not mean that Middle Eastern oil supplies have stopped. Some tankers are reportedly moving with their tracking systems switched off, while Saudi Arabia has increased the amount of crude being exported through the Strait. Saudi exports have risen above 4 million barrels per day in September after falling sharply in August.

articles.title: Hormuz Traffic Falls to Just 12 Commodity Vessels
articles.content: Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz fell sharply over the weekend. Kpler data cited by Reuters showed 12 commodity vessels crossing the Strait, compared with 35 the previous weekend and approximately 125 large commercial vessels per day before the conflict. However, visible vessel traffic does not tell the entire story. Some tankers are reportedly sailing with their Automatic Identification System transponders switched off. Saudi crude exports through the Strait have also recovered above 4 million barrels per day in September, while overall Middle Eastern oil flows remain substantial.
articles.imageQuery: Strait of Hormuz tanker ships satellite

articles.title: Why Hormuz Matters to the Global Economy
articles.content: The Strait of Hormuz is one of the world's most important energy corridors, connecting major Gulf producers with international markets. Prolonged disruption can increase shipping and insurance costs and place pressure on fuel, aviation, manufacturing, transport and household budgets. The latest data also shows why the situation needs to be analysed carefully: shipping has fallen dramatically, but oil is still moving through the region.

articles.title: Macron Backs Canada's Proposed Associate Relationship With EU
articles.content: French President Emmanuel Macron has backed exploring a new associate-member relationship between Canada and the European Union. Macron and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney met in Saint-Pierre and Miquelon and agreed to deepen France-Canada cooperation in areas including energy, defence, space, climate and technology. The proposal is still at the diplomatic stage and does not mean Canada is becoming an EU member.
articles.imageQuery: Emmanuel Macron Mark Carney Canada France meeting

articles.title: Canada–EU Proposal Would Go Beyond Existing Trade Relationship
articles.content: Canada already has a major trade agreement with the European Union, but Ottawa is seeking a broader strategic relationship covering defence and security, energy, critical minerals, artificial intelligence, space, technology, investment and people-to-people links. The proposed associate-member concept would require further negotiations because there is currently no established EU treaty category defining such a status.

articles.title: Trump and Xi Prepare for Washington Summit
articles.content: US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping are preparing for a September 24 meeting in Washington. Their discussions are expected to include tariffs, trade, technology, critical minerals, AI and wider strategic relations. The meeting comes as Washington and Beijing attempt to manage a fragile trade truce and prevent renewed economic tensions from disrupting global supply chains.
articles.imageQuery: Donald Trump Xi Jinping US China summit

articles.title: US and China Begin New AI Security Dialogue
articles.content: US and Chinese officials have agreed to begin discussions on artificial intelligence risks ahead of the Trump–Xi summit. The talks include proposals for greater notification and communication around AI incidents with national-security implications. The development reflects growing concern that advanced AI systems are becoming an issue of international security as well as technology and business.

articles.title: UN General Assembly Brings World Leaders to New York
articles.content: Nearly 130 heads of state are expected in New York this week for the United Nations General Assembly. The meeting comes as governments face simultaneous challenges involving the Middle East, Ukraine, energy security, global trade, humanitarian emergencies and artificial intelligence governance. The gathering will provide an important diplomatic forum for discussions that increasingly cross national borders.

articles.title: Russia Reports Major Drone Attack Around Moscow
articles.content: Russian authorities reported a major Ukrainian drone attack around Moscow during the final day of Russia's parliamentary election. Moscow authorities said hundreds of drones were intercepted and reported deaths and damage, including at an oil refinery. Russia has accused Ukraine of attempting to disrupt the election. Individual battlefield claims and responsibility for specific incidents remain difficult to independently verify.

articles.title: Dangote Adds 4,000 Machines for Refinery Expansion
articles.content: Dangote Industries has acquired an additional 4,000 pieces of construction equipment for its refinery expansion in Lagos, bringing the company's reported construction fleet to about 6,500 machines. The expansion is designed to increase refining capacity from around 700,000 barrels per day towards 1.4 million barrels per day. The company says much of the infrastructure developed for the existing refinery can be reused for the expansion.

articles.title: Dangote IPO Remains One of Africa's Biggest Capital-Market Stories
articles.content: Dangote Petroleum Refinery is offering 4.1 billion shares at ₦525 each in an IPO targeting approximately ₦2.15 trillion, or $1.6 billion at the stated exchange rate. The offer is open until October 13. The refinery reported first-half 2026 net profit of $1.82 billion on revenue above $13 billion and plans to expand capacity towards 1.4 million barrels per day by 2029.
articles.imageQuery: Dangote Refinery IPO Nigeria stock market

articles.title: Reported Southern African Fuel Pipeline Proposal
articles.content: A proposed regional fuel-distribution project linked to Dangote has been reported at an estimated cost of about $3.5 billion, with a planned pipeline network of roughly 2,650 kilometres across Southern Africa. The reported objective is to improve the movement of refined petroleum products to landlocked African markets. The project should be treated as a proposal rather than an operational pipeline, with financing, approvals, construction and commercial arrangements still to be established.

articles.title: Europe Watches Energy Supplies as Middle East Disruption Continues
articles.content: European governments and businesses continue to monitor Middle Eastern energy flows because prolonged shipping disruption can feed into fuel, transport and industrial costs. France has also highlighted the potential importance of Canadian energy supplies, including liquefied natural gas, as Europe considers ways to diversify its energy relationships.

articles.title: Asia Watches US–China Talks and Middle East Energy Flows
articles.content: Asian economies remain closely exposed to developments in Washington, Beijing and the Gulf. Trade restrictions, competition over critical minerals and changes in oil and gas shipping can quickly affect manufacturers, transport operators and consumers across the region. The Trump–Xi summit is therefore being watched well beyond the United States and China.

morningSummary: Good morning. The global energy and geopolitical picture remains unsettled as the Strait of Hormuz records only 12 commodity-vessel crossings over the weekend, down from 35 the previous weekend and far below the roughly 125 large commercial vessels that used the route each day before the conflict. However, oil continues to move through the region, including through tankers operating with tracking systems switched off, and Saudi crude exports through Hormuz have recovered above 4 million barrels per day in September. Meanwhile, Canada and France are deepening their strategic relationship, with Emmanuel Macron supporting exploration of Canada's proposed associate-member relationship with the European Union. In Washington, Donald Trump and Xi Jinping prepare for a September 24 summit, while US and Chinese officials begin new discussions on AI security. In Nigeria, Dangote is expanding its construction fleet and continuing its major refinery expansion and IPO programme.
